products.name: Marketo Optimizer
products.title: Adobe Marketo Optimizer
products.what: Adobe's marketing automation application that runs on your client's Marketo Engage data: programs, people lists and person journeys that send email and WhatsApp messages, with AI that classifies each lead by persona, scores engagement, chooses the next path or the best journey for a person, and a Coworker chat panel that builds and reports in plain language.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Marketo Optimizer documentation (Marketo Optimizer)

products.notes: Marketo Optimizer is its own product in this tool, not Journey Optimizer B2B Edition under a new name. Adobe's pages show the two share a foundation: the setup checklist has administrators create a Journey Optimizer B2B Edition product profile, the permissions sit in Experience Platform under B2B categories, and Adobe says journey traffic control works the same way in both. The difference a partner scopes by is the data and the unit of work: Marketo Optimizer is provisioned on one Marketo Engage instance, in a sandbox named after that subscription, and its journeys are person journeys built on people lists, where the Journey Optimizer B2B Edition lines in this tool (JB01 to JB06) cover B2B schemas, buying groups and account journeys. No service here repeats those. Adobe publishes a product description with a license metric, and its documentation describes what the current release leaves out; every line here rests only on what Adobe documents as working today (see left_out). Much of the daily work runs through the Coworker chat panel, which is written as the moptimizer-cw connection. Adobe says the product is not HIPAA compliant and not HIPAA-ready. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: A Marketo Engage subscription; Adobe connects one Marketo Engage instance as the data source when it provisions Marketo Optimizer
Provisioning finished and the Experience Platform sandbox bound by Adobe; the sandbox is named after your client's Marketo Engage subscription and is added to every role
A system administrator for the Adobe Admin Console and for Permissions in Experience Platform
A sending subdomain that no other Adobe product uses, and your client's DNS team to delegate it
A license sized by profile count, with scoping taken from your client's Marketo Engage purchase
No workloads that need HIPAA compliance; Adobe says the product is not HIPAA compliant and not HIPAA-ready

Customer's scoping parameters shall be based upon the Customer's purchase of Marketo Engage.
Adobe Marketo Optimizer is not HIPAA compliant and not HIPAA-ready

tiers.name: Marketo Optimizer
tiers.what: The base license, measured per 1,000 profiles. It includes up to five sandboxes unless your client licenses more. All lines apply to it; MO09 also needs the WhatsApp entitlement.
tiers.quote: Adobe Marketo Optimizer includes up to 5 Sandboxes, unless licensed separately by Customer.

tiers.name: WhatsApp entitlement
tiers.what: The WhatsApp channel cannot be configured until Adobe has provisioned its entitlement for your client's organization. MO09 needs it.
tiers.quote: Without this entitlement, the WhatsApp channel cannot be configured.

tiers.name: Generative AI credits
tiers.what: The license carries a set number of generative AI credits. Heavy use of the AI features is worth sizing with Adobe before the engagement starts.
tiers.quote: Customer shall receive 500,000 credits for use with the Adobe Marketo Optimizer entitlement.

lines.name: Access, roles and sandbox permissions
lines.scope: Set up access for your client's team: the product profile and user groups in the Admin Console, the administrator, all-access and read-only roles in Experience Platform Permissions with the Marketo Optimizer sandbox on each, and the product permissions each role needs.
lines.evidence: For each user type, you create a user group in the Admin Console and a role in Experience Platform, and then add the group to the role.

source.title: Experience League: User access and permissions (Marketo Optimizer)

lines.name: Email sending setup and channel configurations
lines.scope: Delegate your client's sending subdomain to Adobe with the fully delegated or CNAME method, set the DMARC policy and check SPF and DKIM, review the IP pool, create an email channel configuration for each brand, region and message type, and have IT allowlist the sending addresses.
lines.evidence: Create one or more email channel configurations that bind a subdomain, IP pool, and sender identity.

lines.name: Program types, folders and tokens
lines.scope: Define the program types your client's marketing needs, with their attributes, status steps and success statuses, set up the folder and program structure, and create the My Tokens that folders and programs inherit.
lines.evidence: Program types define important aspects of programs and their members, and distinguish different types of marketing programs from each other.

lines.name: People lists, personas and engagement scoring
lines.scope: Build your client's dynamic and static people lists with filters on activity, company and person attributes, use the derived persona and the person engagement score as filters, and set the engagement score weighting model that fits how your client's leads behave.
lines.evidence: In Adobe Marketo Optimizer, people lists are the person-level audience containers for targeting and person journey entry, with dynamic lists for rule-based live qualification and static lists for fixed or journey-managed membership.

lines.name: First person journeys
lines.scope: Design and publish your client's first person journeys inside their programs: the audience entry by dynamic list or by event, the wait, split and listen-for-event steps, the email actions and data changes, the start and end dates and the re-entry settings, then check each journey before it goes live.
lines.evidence: In Adobe Marketo Optimizer, person journeys are automated, multistep lead-based marketing plans that orchestrate personalized experiences across channels.

lines.name: Email templates, fragments and content rules
lines.scope: Build your client's email templates and reusable visual fragments in the design space, lock the headers, logos and legal content that authors must not change, set up personalization with fallback text, and write the first published emails.
lines.evidence: Content locking allows template authors to define governance rules that restrict which parts of an email template can be modified when the template is used in an email.

source.title: Experience League: Template content governance (Marketo Optimizer)

lines.name: AI path decisions and journey traffic control
lines.scope: Add next best path steps to your client's journeys with a prompt for each path, run simulations on a sample audience and tune the prompts, then turn on journey traffic control for overlapping journeys: the importance of each scoring dimension, the journey descriptions the model reads, and a simulation before the weights go live.
lines.evidence: Journey traffic control (JTC) prioritizes the best journey for a person when audiences overlap.

source.title: Experience League: Journey traffic control (Marketo Optimizer)

lines.name: Landing pages and forms
lines.scope: Set up the landing page subdomain and presets, create the form presets with their streaming connection and dataset in Experience Platform, then build and publish your client's standard forms and the landing pages that carry them.
lines.evidence: Before marketers can create and publish forms to use in their landing pages, a product administrator must create one or more dedicated presets.

lines.name: WhatsApp channel
lines.scope: Connect your client's WhatsApp Business Account: the API credentials, the webhooks with opt-in, opt-out and help keywords and replies, and the channel configuration, then build the first WhatsApp messages from templates Meta has approved and add them to journeys.
lines.evidence: Before marketers can create WhatsApp messages for person journeys, a product administrator must configure a WhatsApp channel.

source.title: Experience League: WhatsApp channel configuration (Marketo Optimizer)

lines.ext: A WhatsApp Business Account with Meta

lines.name: Message frequency and quiet hours rules
lines.scope: Agree with your client how often a person may be contacted and at what hours, build the channel rule sets with frequency caps and quiet hours, activate them and apply them to the email actions in journeys.
lines.evidence: Set frequency caps by channel and communication type to limit how many messages a profile receives and avoid overwhelming customers with similar communications.

lines.name: Send-time optimization and conditional content
lines.scope: Turn on send-time optimization for the email actions where timing matters, with the delivery window and the wait step Adobe requires, and build conditional content rules so one email shows a different block to each persona or segment.
lines.evidence: Use the Send-time optimization (STO) feature to personalize email delivery timing for person journeys by predicting when each profile is most likely to engage.

lines.name: Team training and handover
lines.scope: Train your client's marketers on the home page, the marketing workspace, programs, people lists, journeys and email authoring, with a short guide to your client's naming rules and a checklist for publishing.
lines.evidence: Use the Home page in Adobe Marketo Optimizer to start AI conversations, launch skills, and open marketing workspaces.

lines.name: Monthly journey and audience reviews
lines.scope: Each month, review your client's journey results, email performance, list membership and traffic control decisions, tune audiences, path prompts and score weights, and report findings and next steps.
lines.evidence: Use it in the Coworker chat interface to explore activity trends, email performance, lead and account data, segment and list membership, and journey metrics.

source.title: Experience League: Generate analytics reports (Marketo Optimizer)

connections.how: Marketo Optimizer runs on one Marketo Engage instance, which Adobe connects as its data source when the instance is provisioned. Marketo Engage activities, standard and custom, start person journeys and move people forward in them. Journey actions add people to Marketo Engage static lists, change their status in Marketo Engage programs and request Marketo Engage campaigns. Coworker adapts Marketo Engage smart lists into people lists, and the images in Marketo Engage Design Studio are copied once into the email design space.

client.how: Marketo Optimizer works from your Marketo Engage data. Activity recorded in Marketo Engage, such as a form fill or an email click, starts and advances journeys, and those journeys can add people to your Marketo Engage lists, update their program status and request your Marketo Engage campaigns.
client.gain: You keep your Marketo Engage database, programs and campaigns, and your new journeys react to the same lead activity without a second copy of your data to maintain.

connections.how: Coworker is the chat panel built into Marketo Optimizer. A marketer asks in plain language or picks a skill from the slash menu, and Coworker builds a program from a campaign brief, creates people lists and journeys, drafts emails and answers questions about results. Coworker checks every skill against the permissions the same feature needs outside chat, and creates nothing until the marketer approves.

lines.name: Personas, intent model and AI decisioning data gaps
lines.scope: Prepare the data Marketo Optimizer's AI decisioning reads: define up to 10 personas from your client's person attributes in the persona mapping panel, set and activate the intent model's activity weights with Coworker's Intent configuration skill and check the results with Analyze intent, then use AI-decisioning health to find coverage gaps across demographic, firmographic, technographic, psychographic, persona and intent data and agree an enrichment plan for them.
lines.evidence: Closing those gaps improves how AI decisioning scores and routes each person.

lines.name: Webinar programs with Coworker in Marketo Optimizer
lines.scope: Set up your client's first interactive webinar with Coworker: create the webinar in its program at the licensed capacity, design the registration page and room in the Adobe Connect design surface, build the promotion and post-webinar journeys Coworker drafts, finish what it lists as left to configure (the journey audience, the invitation email, the registration form event filter and the member status steps), test and publish, and leave a reusable webinar program for later events.
lines.evidence: The chat interface lists what is left to configure in the journey canvas.

source.title: Experience League: Create and Promote Webinars (Marketo Optimizer)

client.how: Coworker is the chat panel inside Marketo Optimizer. Your marketers describe what they need or upload a campaign brief, and Coworker sets up the program, lists and journeys for them to review. It can only do what each person's permissions allow, and it creates nothing until that person says to go ahead.
client.gain: Your team starts programs from a brief in one conversation and gets answers about journeys and email results without building a report.

connections.how: Marketo Optimizer sends static people lists to LinkedIn Matched Audience, Google Customer Match and Facebook Custom Audience. An administrator configures each destination by signing in to the ad account. A list is then activated from the People lists page or by an Activate to destination action in a journey, and the destination audience stays in step as people join or leave the list.

not_documented.why: Not a connection. Adobe's pages show the two products share a foundation and name each other, but none describes data moving between them or a setup that joins them. The setup checklist has administrators create a Journey Optimizer B2B Edition product profile, while the user access page calls the same step a Marketo Optimizer product profile, and the journey traffic control page calls the two products tiers of one capability. Written as two separate products; see the trail.
not_documented.quote: Journey traffic control works the same way for both Journey Optimizer B2B Edition and Marketo Optimizer.

not_documented.why: Not found. The guide's 58 pages do not name Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics or a CRM (0 mentions). Opportunity activities and attributes appear as journey triggers and filters, and they arrive through the Marketo Engage data source, which is the existing crm-marketo connection.
not_documented.quote: Activities related to opportunity records associated with leads or accounts.

not_documented.why: Not found. The guide's 58 pages do not name Marketo Measure, Bizible or attribution (0 mentions), and the Marketo Measure guide home does not name Marketo Optimizer. The only tie Adobe states is that both belong to the Marketo product family, on the Marketo Qualifier page.

not_documented.why: No setup documented on a Marketo Optimizer page. The guide overview says Marketo Qualifier can be used with Marketo Optimizer and implements the Account Qualification skill, and journey triggers and filters list lead activities related to Sales Qualifier, but no Optimizer page gives steps to connect the two. The Marketo Qualifier integrations and getting started pages do not name Marketo Optimizer either. The connection is left to the Marketo Qualifier research if its pages document setup.
